# `silk/machine/rules`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Promises a machine keeps on every path, written once with their reason: [`Rules`](#Rules).

## When to use
Use this module for a promise that covers many rows of a chart, such as "reading never
writes a file". Write the promise as a rule, walk the machine with the
`silk.machine.explore` module, and let [`Rules.broken`](#Rules.impl.broken) find every run that breaks it. A
test then fails with the reason of the rule, whatever row caused it.

## Details
A rule is about one event and one effect. It is checked on each run of the event: the step
that takes the event and the steps of the answers of the world that follow it, see
`Walk.runs`. Two effects are the same when `Values.write` writes them as the same text.

Import as `Rules` with `import silk.machine.rules { Rules }`.

<a id="Rules"></a>

## `Rules`

```silk
pub struct Rules<E, C, X>
```

A static table of promises about the effects of a machine with the events `E`, the context
`C` and the effects `X`.

### When to use
Build one in a static function with [`Rules.of`](#Rules.impl.of) and the builders, as a chart is built:
`Rules<Typed, Disk, Mark>.of() |> Rules.never("Read", writes, "reading never writes")`.
Check it with [`Rules.broken`](#Rules.impl.broken).

<a id="Rules.impl.neverWhen"></a>

### Associated function `neverWhen`

```silk
pub static fn neverWhen<G>(
    rules: Rules<E, C, X>,
    event: Intrinsic.VariantName<E>,
    guard: G,
    effect_: X,
    reason: string<'static>,
  ) -> Rules<E, C, X>
```

Adds the promise that no run of `event` leaves `effect_` when `guard` holds, for the
reason `reason`. `guard` is a function `fn(&C, &E) -> bool` or a `Guard`. It sees the
context as it was before the event, and the event.

<a id="Rules.impl.applying"></a>

### Associated function `applying`

```silk
pub effect fn applying(
    static rules: Rules<E, C, X>,
    context: &C,
    event: &E,
    reasons: &mut List<string<'static>>,
  ) -> ()
    ! OutOfMemoryError
    ? &mut Allocator
```

Appends to `reasons` the reason of each rule of `rules` that is about `event` and whose
guard holds for `context` and `event`, in the order of the table.

<a id="Rules.impl.broken"></a>

### Associated function `broken`

```silk
pub effect fn broken<S: Machine<E, C, X>>(
    static rules: Rules<E, C, X>,
    walk: &Walk<S, E, C, X>,
    runs: &[Run],
    events: &[E],
  ) -> List<Broken>
    ! OutOfMemoryError
    ? &mut Allocator
```

Returns the runs of `runs` that break a rule of `rules`, each with the reason of the
rule it breaks.

#### Details
`walk` is the walk the runs come from, see `Walk.runs`, and `events` the list of events
the walk was made with. A rule is checked on a run when it is about the event of the
first step of the run and its guard holds for the context the run starts from.
